# How the javascript parser decides

<!-- generated by `node test/decision-report.ts --write` from the portable plan (src/emit-portable.ts) of `javascript.ts`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every choice point of the grammar and how the generated parser (the portable plan every target prints) decides it: by one token, by two tokens, by attempt (an ordered choice tries its branches in order; a repetition without a FIRST guard tries its body), or by longest match in a candidate frame; and whether it takes a mark that a failure restores. Then the findings a grammar author should act on, each with its witness. How it is derived: test/decision-report.ts.

## Findings

### Dead alternatives

None.

### Ties decided by declaration order

Two candidates of one list match the same input to the same end; the one declared first wins. Where the later one is meant to win there, the grammar must say so (reorder, or refuse the token in the earlier one). "One token": both can match exactly one token at these tokens (the witness is that token parsed as the rule, where the engine observes the tie). "Observed": a frame on the pinned inputs where they tied (how often, and the first place).
